chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Salamah al-Hannat, who said:
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: “What is your occupation?” I said: “A grain seller, and sometimes I come upon brisk demand, and sometimes I come upon stagnation, so I hold it back.”
He said: “What do the people around you say about it?” I said: “They say: a hoarder.” He said: “Does anyone other than you sell it?”

I said: “What I sell is only one part out of a thousand parts.” So he said: “There is no harm. Rather, that concerned a man from Quraysh called Hakim ibn Hizam. When food entered al-Madinah, he would buy all of it. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed by him and said to him: ‘O Hakim ibn Hizam, beware lest you hoard.’”

key_terms.إِيَّاكَ: beware; a warning of prohibition or serious avoidance
key_terms.الطَّعَامُ: food supply entering the city market
key_terms.تَحْتَكِرَ: to engage in hoarding or monopolistic withholding
key_terms.فَحَبَسْتُهُ: so I withheld it from immediate sale
key_terms.مُحْتَكِرٌ: one who hoards goods, especially food, to the harm of the market
key_terms.نَفَاقٍ: brisk market demand and ready sale

ai.seo_question: When does holding back food for sale count as forbidden hoarding in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses hoarding in trade and distinguishes between ordinary commercial holding and harmful monopoly. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام explains that blameworthy hoarding is when a person buys up the market supply, as in the case of Hakim ibn Hizam, preventing others from access to food.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3957 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Salamah al-Hannat, who said that

Abu Abdullah (as), asked: "What is your occupation?"
I replied: "I am a wheat seller, and sometimes I arrive during a time of demand, and sometimes I arrive during a time of stagnation, so I hold onto it."

Imam (as) asked: "What do the people around you say about this?"
I said: "They say I am a hoarder."
Imam (as) then asked: "Do others besides you sell it?"

I said: "I sell only a small portion compared to the whole market."
Imam (as) replied: "There is no harm in that. This issue arose with a man from Quraysh named Hakim ibn Hizam. Whenever food entered Medina, he would buy all of it.
The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, passed by him and said: 'O Hakim ibn Hizam, beware of hoarding.'"
